batchName: Late Republic: Antony, Octavian and the End of the Republic (44-27 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Late Republic: Antony, Octavian and the End of the Republic (44-27 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What did Romans call the Mediterranean, Mare Nostrum?
questions.explanation: After Actium and Alexandria, Octavian controlled all of it.

questions.question: Augustus’s rule began the Pax Romana. What was it?
questions.explanation: Historians see 27 BC as the end of the Republic and the start of the empire.
questions.sourceQuote: and of the long Roman Peace (*Pax Romana*).

questions.question: Augustus ruled as princeps. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: He kept the outward forms of the republic, much as the triumvirs had.
questions.sourceQuote: He ruled as first citizen (*princeps*) while keeping the outward forms of the republic

questions.question: Who kept Antony’s will in Rome?
options: The virgines Vestales, priestesses of the sacred hearth
questions.explanation: Octavian seized it and read it out; historians suspect he invented some of it.
questions.sourceQuote: kept by the Vestal Virgins (*virgines Vestales*), the priestesses of Rome's sacred hearth.

questions.question: Who were the equites killed in the proscriptions alongside senators?
options: Knights, the wealthy class just below the senators
questions.explanation: One modern study settles on about 300 names, split evenly between senators and knights.
questions.sourceQuote: plus many knights (*equites*), the wealthy class just below the senators.

questions.question: What did the lex Titia of 27 November 43 BC do?
options: Gave the three men their power for five years
questions.explanation: It was close to absolute rule: they could even appoint every magistrate.
questions.sourceQuote: A friendly tribune passed a law, the *lex Titia*, on 27 November 43 BC, giving them this power for five years.

questions.question: What was the official name of the three men’s board, the triumviri rei publicae constituendae?
options: The board of three for restoring the republic
The board of three for war
questions.explanation: We call it the Second Triumvirate, a modern label first used in the 17th century.
questions.sourceQuote: The three men named themselves the board of three for restoring the republic (*triumviri rei publicae constituendae*).

questions.question: What did Caesar’s killers call themselves?
questions.explanation: At first an uneasy compromise held: the assassins were pardoned.
questions.sourceQuote: His killers called themselves the liberators (*liberatores*).
